title: Towards Agentic Scientific Discovery in Distributed Systems
abstract: arXiv:2611.20031v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We investigate when adaptive tool selection helps identify a shared equation across clients with different input coverage. Query-ATLAS (query-conditioned Agentic Tool-based Learning for Aggregating Symbolic Equations) uses an LLM to guide symbolic search from client errors and previous proposals in a simulated distributed system. A four-architecture comparison reveals task-dependent opportunities: relative to fixed PySR-LLM, validation acceptances rise from 3/12 to 7/12 on CRK3 and from 11/12 to 12/12 on oscillator2, while MatSci3 favors the fixed workflow. Across 72 settings in a post-hoc six-task subset of eight development tasks, Query-ATLAS achieves 64 validation and 64 in-distribution passes, versus 62 and 59 for the fixed workflow; both pass 47/60 eligible out-of-distribution tests. translated_title: 迈向分布式系统中的智能体式科学发现
translated_abstract: 我们研究了自适应工具选择在何种情况下有助于识别具有不同输入覆盖范围的多个客户端之间的共享方程。Query-ATLAS（基于查询条件的智能体工具学习，用于聚合符号方程）利用大语言模型（LLM）在模拟分布式系统中，根据客户端误差和先前的提案来引导符号搜索。四种架构的对比揭示了依赖于任务的机会：相对于固定的PySR-LLM工作流，验证通过数在CRK3上从3/12提升至7/12，在oscillator2上从11/12提升至12/12，而MatSci3则更倾向于固定工作流。在八个开发任务中事后选取的六任务子集的72种设置下，Query-ATLAS实现了64次验证通过和64次分布内通过，而固定工作流分别为62次和59次；两者均通过了60项符合条件的分布外测试中的47项。固定工作流仍保持更低的中位数误差和成本。更广泛的查询覆盖展现出有前景的优势，这也为任务感知的工具选择提供了动力。
tldr: Query-ATLAS利用LLM在模拟分布式系统中根据客户端误差和先前提案引导符号搜索，通过自适应工具选择在部分任务上显著提升跨客户端共享方程的识别成功率，同时表明工具选择应具备任务感知能力。
en_tdlr: Query-ATLAS leverages an LLM to guide symbolic search from client errors and prior proposals in a simulated distributed system, showing that adaptive tool selection boosts shared-equation discovery on some tasks and motivates task-aware tool selection.
